title: Seed sounds on the petals
hookLine: anatomy posters label organs; this old map writes letters on its petals
carry: in a mantra, the sound itself is sacred
tomorrow: a moon on the left, a sun on the right. what runs between?

lines: THIS MAP WRITES LETTERS ON PETALS.
cards: Anatomy posters label things: thighbone, artery, nerve. The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana labels its map too, but strangely. Each lotus along the spine has letters of the Sanskrit alphabet set on its petals.
At its center sits a shape and a seed sound, and inside, a god and a goddess. No one has ever drawn an organ like that. So why would a map of the body carry an alphabet?

teach.b: Because it isn't a map of the body's parts. It's a map for the mind on the way up, and it's built of sound.

That's one of Hinduism's oldest convictions: sound itself can be sacred. The Vedas were kept for centuries by ear, memorized syllable by syllable, because how they sounded mattered as much as what they meant.
A mantra works the same way: it's said for its sound, not only translated. Here each lotus has a bija at its center, a seed syllable.

teach.h: BIJA: LAM AT THE ROOT, HAM AT THE THROAT.
teach.b: The text gives the root lotus lam, and the throat lotus ham. They aren't words with a dictionary meaning. They're seeds, said inwardly.

teach.h: MATRIKA: THE LETTERS AS LITTLE MOTHERS.
teach.b: And many tantric teachers call the letters of the alphabet matrika, little mothers, forms of the Goddess herself. So the letters on the petals aren't labels. They're the climb, sounded out.

Here's the line worth taking to dinner: the old map is drawn with an alphabet, not a scalpel. Some modern writers have tried to line the lotuses up with glands or bundles of nerves. The old map never asked for that.
Read on its own terms, the puzzle solves itself.

teach.h: A PLACE TO REST, AND LISTEN.
teach.b: Letters on petals means this is a place for the mind to rest, and listen.

how: Many Hindus chant Om and other mantras aloud or inwardly; in tantric meditation on the chakras, practitioners picture each lotus with its petals and letters and repeat its seed syllable inwardly, as the texts describe and a teacher guides.

games.q: what does “the chakras as a map” mean?
o: a map drawn with letters and sound, for the mind
a spelling chart for learning Sanskrit
a code that names each gland in Sanskrit

some modern writers have tried that; the text describes what to picture and hear in meditation.
in the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana, the lotuses carry letters on their petals
and a seed sound at each center: things for the mind to hold.
a mantra only works if you know what each syllable means in English

games.q: a friend says chanting a syllable you can't translate is pointless. what would today's teaching say?
o: in Hindu practice the sound itself is sacred; a seed syllable is said, not translated.
she's right: if it can't be translated, it's just noise.
only the letters' shapes matter; saying them adds nothing.
games.why: the Vedas were kept by ear, syllable by syllable, and each lotus here holds a seed sound. the sound is the practice.

practice: Sit tall. Say Om slowly, out loud, three times, letting each one fade before the next. Then say it inwardly, once with each out-breath, for the rest of the sit.
If Om isn't yours to say, hum one low, steady note instead, and listen to it end.

wordCard.voice: The chakras as a map: lotuses with letters on their petals and a seed sound at the center, drawn for the mind, not for the scalpel.

orig.note: Sanskrit: seed; a seed syllable, the sound at the center of each lotus.
